title: The Bank Heist a Printer Hid

scenes.narration: [serious] Hackers tried to steal almost a billion dollars. A printer hid it. [short pause] In February 2016, thieves broke into the central bank of Bangladesh.
[whispers] They sent thirty-five fake payment orders to the New York Fed. The total was about 951 million dollars.
[serious] Five payments went through. [pause] One hundred and one million dollars was gone.
Why did nobody notice? The bank's printer printed every transfer. The hackers had tampered with it. On Friday morning, the paper tray was empty.
Staff tried the New York Fed by email, phone and fax. It was the weekend. Nobody answered.

shots.at: Staff tried the New York Fed

scenes.narration: One payment was stopped. A bank noticed a spelling mistake in the name. The word was Fandation, not Foundation.
But 81 million dollars went to four accounts in the Philippines. Then it vanished into casinos.
In 2018, U.S. prosecutors charged a North Korean programmer, Park Jin Hyok. Only about 15 million dollars was ever recovered. One small typo saved the rest.

facts.claim: 35 fraudulent SWIFT orders, about $951 million, sent to the New York Fed on Feb 4, 2016
Five payments worth $101 million were paid; $81 million went to four Philippine accounts
Printer tray empty on Friday Feb 5 morning; hackers tampered with printer software
$20 million to 'Shalika Fandation' was stopped after a bank questioned the misspelling
DOJ charged Park Jin Hyok in June 2018; about $15 million of the $81 million recovered
